title.en: Use count, index and built-ins on tuples
Swap and unpack with tuple assignment

say.en: Swapping two values usually needs a third, temporary variable. With tuple assignment, Python swaps them in one line. In this lesson: Use count, index and built-ins on tuples.
Swap and unpack with tuple assignment.
Access nested tuples.

body.en: Tuples have only two methods: count(x) and index(x). *Built-in functions* len(), tuple(), min(), max(), sum() and sorted() also work on tuples. tuple() converts a sequence such as a list or string into a tuple. sorted() returns a list.
body.kn: ಟ್ಯೂಪಲ್‌ಗೆ count(x) ಮತ್ತು index(x) ಎಂಬ ಎರಡೇ ಮೆಥಡ್‌ಗಳು. len(), tuple(), min(), max(), sum(), sorted() ಕೂಡ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ. sorted() ಲಿಸ್ಟ್ ಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Tuple assignment a, b = b, a packs the right side into a tuple first and then unpacks it, so the values swap with no extra variable. A nested tuple is a tuple of tuples: t[i] picks a row, t[i][j] one item. Swap twice. Where are the values now? Which index gives 8? Say it before you choose.
narration.kn: ಟ್ಯೂಪಲ್ ನಿಯೋಜನೆ a, b = b, a ಬಲಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಮೊದಲು ಟ್ಯೂಪಲ್ ಮಾಡಿ ನಂತರ ಬಿಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ; ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಚರವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಮೌಲ್ಯಗಳು ಅದಲುಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಅಂತರ್ಗತ ಟ್ಯೂಪಲ್ ಎಂದರೆ ಟ್ಯೂಪಲ್‌ಗಳ ಟ್ಯೂಪಲ್: t[i] ಒಂದು ಸಾಲು, t[i][j] ಒಂದು ಅಂಶ. ಎರಡು ಬಾರಿ ಅದಲುಬದಲು ಮಾಡಿ. ಮೌಲ್ಯಗಳು ಈಗ ಎಲ್ಲಿ? ಯಾವ ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ 8 ಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ? ಆರಿಸುವ ಮೊದಲು ಹೇಳಿ.

title.en: On the board: Tuple assignment and swapping

say.en: Tuple assignment gives each variable on the left the value in the same position on the right.
This lets us swap two variables without a third one. The right side is packed first, then unpacked.
The counts on both sides must match, or Python raises a ValueError.
A nested tuple is a tuple inside a tuple. n of 1 is the inner tuple 3, 4, and n of 1 of 0 is 3.
Only two methods: count and index. sorted of a tuple returns a list.

myth.en: t = ("Asha") makes a tuple with one name in it.

truth.en: It makes the string "Asha". Write t = ("Asha",) with a trailing comma. Round brackets are also used to group expressions, as in (2 + 3) * 4. It is the comma, not the brackets, that makes a tuple.

say.en: A tuple is an ordered, immutable sequence; the comma makes it a tuple.
One-element tuple: (5,).
Tuple methods: count and index only; sorted() returns a list.
Tuple assignment evaluates the right side first: a, b = b, a swaps.
Unpacking needs as many variables as values, else ValueError.

explain.en: sorted() always returns a new list, whatever sequence it is given. Use tuple(sorted(t)) to get a tuple back.

task.en: Which of these is a tuple?

question.en: Which of these is a tuple?

explain.en: The comma makes a tuple: 7, is the tuple (7,). (7) is just the number 7, and [7] is a list.

takeaway.en: A tuple is an ordered, immutable sequence; the comma makes it a tuple.

headline.en: "List vs tuple": list is mutable, uses [ ], has methods like append and sort; tuple is immutable, uses ( ), has only count and index, and is slightly faster and safer for fixed data. Remember that a tuple containing a list can still have that inner list changed: (1, [2, 3])[1].append(4) works.

narration.en: Many people think: t = ("Asha") makes a tuple with one name in it. Actually: It makes the string "Asha". Write t = ("Asha",) with a trailing comma. Round brackets are also used to group expressions, as in (2 + 3) * 4. It is the comma, not the brackets, that makes a tuple.

st equals (("Asha", 92), ("Ravi", 85), ("Meena", 78)).
for i in range(lenst).
name, marks equals st[i].
print(i plus 1, name, marks).
Each inner tuple is unpacked into name and marks by tuple assignment.

2 Ravi 85
